Summary: The respect law: rise before gray hair and honor the aged, treating age itself as worthy of deference.
Commandment: Stand up in the presence of gray hair and honor the aged.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as moral. Paul applies the same posture inside the church: treat older men as fathers and older women as mothers, correcting with gentleness.
Purpose: Leviticus 19:32 commands rising before gray hair as reverence for age itself; Paul applies the posture inside the church (1 Timothy 5:1-2).
